rationale:
The example `requirements.sdk.graph.search.utf8_window` describes a concrete case. A file-root item contains `éhit猫` with no header or trailer. With `window_bytes: 2`, the excerpt is `éhit...`. With the default window, the excerpt is `éhit猫`. The returned match is `{"tag":"1","node":…,"excerpt":…}`.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[root_hits_clip_context_to_utf8_boundaries]` carries a `{test}` reference to the example. It covers the scenario as follows:
- **Setup:** it writes `éhit猫` to `fragment.rs`, which the test treats as the file-root item `fragment.rs#`. The test project is built from that same text. It searches for the pattern `hit`.
- **Small window:** it dispatches `search_text` with `window_bytes: 2` and expects the excerpt `éhit...`. This checks that the two bytes before `hit` keep the whole `é`. It also checks that the two bytes after `hit` fall partway into `猫`, so that context is dropped and the `...` marker is appended directly at the cut.
- **Default window:** it dispatches `search_text` with no `window_bytes` and expects the excerpt `éhit猫`. This checks that the default 128-byte window covers the item, so the excerpt is the original text.
- **Output shape:** both calls assert `page["matches"]` equals the single entry `{"tag":"1","node":<the node of fragment.rs#>,"excerpt":expected}`. This checks the tag and the node. The example's literal node `10` is an arbitrary interned id, so comparing against the interned node is the right check.
- **Extra checks:** it reads the node back and checks that the full text is `éhit猫` and that the node read was `fragment.rs#`.

The extra `needle` iteration in the test is harmless. The test asserts every outcome the example states. I found no behavior that would satisfy these tests while violating the example or the cited `windows` and `omissions` requirements.

text: A file-root item contains `éhit猫` and has no header or trailer. With `window_bytes: 2`, the agent receives `{"tag":"1","node":10,"excerpt":"éhit..."}`. The two bytes before `hit` contain the entire `é`. The two bytes after it cover only part of `猫`, so the excerpt ends with the omission marker. With the default window, the excerpt is `éhit猫`.

The agent's `search_text` tool accepts a nonnegative `window_bytes`, defaulting to 128. For a hit with byte span `[start, end)`, retain the hit and up to `window_bytes` of source immediately before `start` and after `end`. Clip the window to the enclosing item's span. Move a context boundary that splits a UTF-8 character inward to the nearest character boundary. With `window_bytes: 0`, only the hit spans and the available header and trailer contribute source to the excerpt.

Compute windows for all hits in the item from the same snapshot. Where windows touch or overlap, emit the contiguous source once. This preserves each hit and the text between nearby hits, including whitespace and newlines.

Render the union of the header, hit windows, and trailer in source order. Copy retained bytes verbatim and replace each nonempty omitted region of the enclosing item with the literal `...`, including a gap at the beginning or end. Insert the marker directly at the cut. When the retained spans cover the item, the excerpt is its original text.
